text: Continuous integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. Whenever a developer adds new code to a shared project, an automated build starts immediately. The system compiles the code and runs tests automatically, so the team does not have to do this by hand. This helps catch issues early, while they are still easy and cheap to fix. A CI pipeline usually includes several stages, such as building, testing, and reporting results. If something fails, the team gets a clear warning straight away. In short, CI makes software development faster, safer, and more reliable for everyone.
